title: Adab of sleep
hook: the one thing no one can do on purpose, and the remembrance that goes with it

segments.voice: Yesterday, the adab of travel, and your line: travel remembering. Today, the shortest journey of every day: the one into sleep.

Lights off. Phone face down. And then the one thing in the day nobody can do on purpose: fall asleep. You can't push your way into it. You can only lie down and let go. The Qur'an treats that letting go as no small thing. In surah al-Zumar, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah receiveth (men's) souls at the time of their death, and that (soul) which dieth not (yet) in its sleep." Every night, something is handed over. Today: handing it over well.
screen: `LIGHTS OFF.` → `NOBODY FALLS ASLEEP ON PURPOSE.` → `EVERY NIGHT, A HANDING OVER.`

segments.voice: Start with al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, told him, in paraphrase: when you go to your bed, make wudu as you would for prayer, lie down on your right side, and say a short du'a handing yourself over to Allah. Make it your last words, he said. If you die that night, you die on the fitrah, the natural state. The body washed, laid down a particular way, and the last words of the day chosen, not left to whatever was on the screen. Some of this you met on day one hundred thirty-six. Then 'A'ishah adds what she saw night after night, also in Bukhari: he cupped his hands, blew into them lightly, and recited the three short surahs at the end of the Qur'an, al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas, the three quls, each beginning with qul, say. Then he wiped his hands over as much of his body as he could, starting with his head and face, three times. Last, two sentences from Hudhayfah, in Bukhari. Lying down: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. Waking, in paraphrase: praise to Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the rising. Sleep, a small dying. Waking, a small rising. The verse from al-Zumar, folded into two lines a person can say in the dark.
screen: `WUDU, THEN THE RIGHT SIDE.` · `LAST WORDS, CHOSEN.` · `THREE QULS INTO CUPPED HANDS.` · `IN YOUR NAME I DIE AND I LIVE.`

segments.voice: Rehearse tonight: water on your hands and face, wudu or simply washing, then lying down on your right side. If you know al-Ikhlas, say it slowly in your mind, qul huwa Allahu ahad, and if you pray, plan for your last words to be bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya, in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. If you don't, choose one thing from today to set down before you sleep, and see yourself setting it down.
Adab of sleep. The manners of lying down: wudu, the right side, the three quls, and a last word of remembrance before the day lets go. Today's word.
Your line: sleep with remembrance. Each night a small dying, each morning a small rising. Tomorrow, the manners of learning.

howItsDone: Muslims follow the Prophet's bedtime practice: making wudu, lying on the right side, reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas into cupped hands and wiping over the body, and saying "bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya" before sleep.

what a scholar hears: 'in Your name I die and I live' (Bukhari 6312) beside al-Zumar 39:42: the soul taken in sleep and returned on waking.

chat.says: What do Muslims say right before falling asleep?
options: One short line: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. Often after the three quls.
Nothing special. The Prophet kept bedtime silent, with no words at all.
A long prayer of at least an hour, or the sleep doesn't count.
chat.meaning: Hudhayfah reports that lying down, the Prophet said: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. 'A'ishah saw him recite the three quls.

fitrah.meaning: the natural state a person is created in

quls.meaning: the three short surahs that begin with qul, say

al-Zumar.meaning: a surah of the Qur'an, The Crowds
